findings.impact: This is reproducible as a chosen tied-width assumption, but the adapter says every architecture parameter is explicit and the contract asks for a configurable graph. The current mapping does not independently express the unresolved projection or fusion-gate hidden widths. This is not evidence that the chosen widths differ from the original.

findings.status_at_snapshot: Resolved in concurrent uncommitted adapter edit; valid world-size admission still depends on actual source-qualified fit membership.
findings.classification: concrete training dataflow issue found and blocked by admission rule
findings.evidence: local_sequence_indices pads each rank to equal length with -1. SequenceDataset.__getitem__(-1) returns an all-zero sequence and mask, collate includes it, and GALAMSequenceAdapter normalizes all values before calling the model. PerTimeBatchNorm1d uses every row and receives no membership/loss mask. A fit of 7 sequences at world_size 2 and batch_size 2 would have passed the singleton checks while placing a zero-weight sentinel in a two-row BatchNorm batch. The latest adapter edit rejects fit_sequences % world_size != 0 before model construction.
findings.impact: Without the new guard, the zero-loss padding row would change normalized activations and BatchNorm statistics for real rows. Current admission blocks that case by requiring a world size that divides the actual fitting membership.
findings.smallest_correction: Implemented in the concurrent adapter edit: reject nondivisible fit membership and retain the existing batch_size >= 2 and no-singleton-tail checks. Confirm the real source-qualified sequence count before selecting an admitted world size.

remaining_source_gaps: No public original GALAM repository, technical report, source checkpoint, or complete original training recipe was found in the bounded source scout; the supplied local images and author observation text are the implementation evidence.

The diagram and text do not settle width, head count, block counts, attention cache/window semantics, convolution kernel and hidden width, timestamp scale/source, BatchNorm axis and running-stat convention, fusion gate equation/order/bypass operand, hidden/cell projection widths, and FFN widths.
The author text names a GeGLU MLP-Mixer while the supplied global diagram depicts ConvMixer; retain this conflict as unresolved and do not silently equate them.
The Connectome 112-to-2 sequence adapter adds train-only external normalization and an empty hint output; adapter docstring says these are runtime adaptations, not claims about the original model.
The author reports SWA and a four-model FiLM ensemble, but the inspected package is a single-model architecture/adapter and does not reproduce those training/submission steps or reported scores.

The decoder image establishes a multiplication node and its position but does not specify the bypass equation; the author note describes two sigmoid gates. The implementation selects one 4*width sigmoid vector over a four-source concatenation. Gate grouping and the exact bypass operand remain assumed.
The current gate hidden width (4*width) and hidden/cell projection widths are tied in code rather than separate required config fields; the selected widths do not establish source parity.
The actual source-qualified fit count is not available in this read-only snapshot, so admission for the desired 8-GPU world size cannot yet be established.
